source.title: EraseSAE: Surgical Concept Erasure in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xing-Hao Wang; Dong Li; Wei Yu; Ying-Wei Pan; Tao Gong; Qi Chu; Neng-Hai Yu; Ting Yao

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoder features as units for concept erasure and relies on their claimed semantic interpretability, but does not test the claim about the share or usefulness of the model's own neurons.
record.gate_note: The study's results concern learned SAE feature kernels and concept-erasure performance, not the interpretability of the model's own neurons. Its neuron-level polysemanticity statements are arguments, not measurements. The one feature-purity result retained is related to the claim's subject but does not test any listed version; erasure benchmark results do not measure neuron interpretability.
record.test_reason: The study builds a sparse autoencoder (PConvSAE) for concept erasure in text-to-video diffusion models. It reports only erasure and preservation performance, plus the purity of its own learned SAE kernels. It asserts that neurons are polysemantic but never measures the model's own neurons. So no version, about neuron shares, canonical examples, neuron circuits or explanation scoring, is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that EraseSAE, which uses PConvSAE plus contrastive attribution and spatially-modulated guidance, achieves state-of-the-art localized concept erasure with minimal quality loss. They describe this as moving intervention from polysemantic neurons to monosemantic features. Their claim that neurons are polysemantic is assumed, not measured.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a convolutional sparse autoencoder and feature-level attribution for text-to-video concept erasure, rather than auditing neuron poles or testing neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-purity comparison differs by SAE architecture: PConvSAE versus linear SAE.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned convolutional SAE concept kernels show higher purity than linear SAE features for celebrity identities. Purity is averaged over 5 identities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this study's PConvSAE, trained with a leakage penalty in text-to-video diffusion models, concept kernels reach mean purity 0.76 versus 0.37 for a linear SAE. These are SAE features, not neurons.

record.problems: The study does not directly test neuron interpretability. The reported purity comparison is an aggregate over five identities, with no uncertainty reported and no model-specific breakdown stated in that passage.
record.rows_left_out: Concept-erasure benchmark, ablation, and preservation results in Tables 1–6 were not extracted because they measure erasure performance rather than neuron interpretability or the listed versions.

untested.parts: No neuron-level audit in any model. The models studied (CogVideoX-5B, HunyuanVideo, Flux.1) are diffusion models, not language models.
No examination of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No measurement of interpretable-neuron share across tools or architectures. The neuron-level polysemanticity statement in the introduction is asserted, not measured.
No attribution graphs built from model neurons.
No test of neuron explanations against held-out activations.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron polysemanticity statements appear in the introduction and conclusion as motivation only, with no neuron measurements. The record's T4/uses_without_test classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job counts.
No cross-model or scale audit of neuron poles.
No test of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
No estimate of interpretable neuron shares across architectures or tools.
No attribution-graph test using model neurons.
No test of explanations against activations beyond their activating examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: PConvSAE concept kernels (celebrity identity results; five-identity average)
rows.operation_detail: Measures semantic purity of locked concept kernels; compares with a linear SAE.
rows.note: The study reports the average over five identities but does not provide model-specific values here. This measures learned SAE kernels, not the model's own neurons.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (PConvSAE kernels, 0.76) with a linear SAE (0.37). The units are learned SAE features, not model neurons. The SAE was also trained with a leakage penalty that pushes for purity. It is a method-performance comparison and should not be read as evidence on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
